title: building on ARM on Windows fails on gettext
body: I imported the project into Visual Studio 2022 ARM64. It compiles, but the target is x86 rather than ARM64. I probably need to modify the CMake configuration, but I am not a developer and do not know how. I would like instructions for compiling Neovim for ARM on Windows.

symptoms_visible: Visual Studio 2022 on my ARM64 machine compiles the project as x86 instead of ARM64.
N0.label: N0 x86 target produced on ARM64 host

symptoms_visible: I am building on an ARM machine, but the Visual Studio CMake project does not offer ARM64 as a target and my command-line GCC attempt also produces the wrong architecture.
N1.label: N1 native ARM host and target-selection problem confirmed

symptoms_visible: The command-line build now invokes the Hostarm64/arm64 MSVC compiler and gets through other dependencies, but gettext stops while compiling localename.c and langprefs.c.
MSVC's stdint.h reports error C2632 on lines declaring an '__int64' followed by 'long'.
N2.label: N2 native MSVC ARM64 build isolated to gettext

symptoms_visible: After applying the proposed gettext CMake patch, the ARM64 build completes past the gettext failure.
When I run the resulting binary, it reports E5113 because module 'vim.uri' cannot be found.
N3.label: N3 gettext patch works on tested source revision

symptoms_visible: After setting VIMRUNTIME to the source runtime directory, the built ARM64 Neovim starts without the missing vim.uri error.
N4.label: N4 locally built ARM64 binary runs

symptoms_visible: After updating to the latest source and applying the same local patch, the dependency build still stops instead of producing the ARM64 build.
N4_x.label: N4_x old local patch fails on newer source

symptoms_visible: I have not reported a retest of the merged upstream fix on my ARM64 Windows machine; my last test of the older local patch against the latest source still stopped during the build.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal upstream fix reported merged without reporter retest

question_patterns: Are you building on an ARM Windows machine, or cross-compiling from an x86 machine?
Can you confirm the architecture of the machine running the build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am on an ARM machine, so I am trying to build natively rather than cross-compile from x86.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am actually running the build on an x64 Windows machine and want it to emit ARM64 binaries.

question_patterns: What target options does Visual Studio offer for this CMake project?
Can you select ARM64 from Visual Studio's target menu?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not let me choose an ARM target for this CMake project. A new desktop app project lets me select ARM64, but a new CMake project does not.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: ARM64 is available in the target menu, and selecting it produces a native ARM64 build without an error.
The target is listed as ARM64 in a different Visual Studio submenu, but selecting it still leaves the generated compiler as x86.

question_patterns: Have you tried building from the command line, and which compiler did it use?
Does a command-line build produce the expected architecture?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I also tried the command line with GCC, but it produced the wrong target. I do not know how to force ARM64, and GCC appears not to support the Windows ARM64 target I need.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c5, reporter yashamon's system: maintainers first distinguished unsupported cross-compilation from a native build. The reporter confirmed an ARM host and described the missing Visual Studio CMake target plus the GCC attempt.

question_patterns: Can you run the documented build from an ARM64-native MSVC command prompt and paste the compiler summary?
Once the native toolchain is selected, which compiler path does CMake report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I got the command-line build further. The summary reports C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/2022/Community/VC/Tools/MSVC/14.40.33807/bin/Hostarm64/arm64/cl.exe as the C compiler, with Target system: Windows.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The summary still points to Hostx64/x86/cl.exe rather than an ARM64 compiler.
The selected compiler is a different MSVC toolset version, but its path is still Hostarm64/arm64/cl.exe.

question_patterns: What is the first concrete error from the native ARM64 build?
Please paste the failing dependency command and the compiler diagnostics.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The build stops in the gettext step while compiling gettext-runtime/intl/localename.c and langprefs.c. MSVC reports stdint.h(45) and stdint.h(46): error C2632: '__int64' followed by 'long' is illegal.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Gettext builds successfully; the first failure is instead a linker error for libuv with an x86/ARM64 machine-type mismatch.
The same C2632 diagnostics occur in another gettext source file but still point into MSVC's stdint.h.

question_patterns: Can you build LuaJIT by itself using its Windows build instructions and report the raw result?
Does the standalone LuaJIT ARM64 build fail on this platform?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can build LuaJIT on ARM Windows with msvcbuild. The output generates vm_arm64.dasc and compiles with LUAJIT_TARGET=LUAJIT_ARCH_ARM64; the Neovim failure I am seeing is in gettext.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The standalone LuaJIT build fails before producing its ARM64 objects, with the same failure seen inside the Neovim dependency build.

edges.comment: Issue c11-c15 and c19. The ARM64 MSVC compiler summary and gettext C2632 log are from reporter yashamon. The standalone LuaJIT result is from affected participant Daydreamer-riri and is folded into the simulated user side; it rules out the earlier LuaJIT suspicion without mixing a different deployment into the gettext failure.

solution.intent: Correct Neovim's generated gettext configuration for MSVC so it uses the integer types supplied by stdint.h instead of injecting the non-MSVC uintmax_t/intmax_t fallback.
solution.concrete_example: In GettextCMakeLists.txt, add an MSVC branch that defines HAVE_STDINT_H_WITH_UINTMAX and HAVE_STDINT_H, and keep the hand-written uintmax_t/intmax_t fallback only in the non-MSVC branch. Reconfigure from a clean dependency build directory and rebuild with the ARM64 MSVC toolchain.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the ARM64 compiler path and the C2632 diagnostics from MSVC's stdint.h. Identifying Neovim's generated gettext config as the source of conflicting fallback integer declarations is engineer-side inference embodied by the patch in c26.

edges.comment: Issue c26-c28, reporter yashamon's system: jxy-s proposed the MSVC-specific gettext configuration patch, and yashamon confirmed that it worked for the dependency build. The subsequent vim.uri runtime error was a separate observable consequence of launching from the build tree, not evidence against the gettext diagnosis.

solution.intent: Point the locally built Neovim executable at the source runtime directory so its bundled Lua runtime modules can be found during an uninstalled-tree launch.
solution.concrete_example: Set VIMRUNTIME to the repository's runtime directory before launching the locally built executable.

edges.comment: Issue c27-c28, reporter yashamon's system: after the gettext patch allowed the build to complete, the reporter resolved the separate uninstalled-runtime launch error by setting VIMRUNTIME. This edge records that persistent environment change but does not make it part of the scored gettext root cause.

solution.intent: Reuse the original local gettext CMake patch unchanged after updating to the latest Neovim source.
solution.concrete_example: Update the checkout and apply the same MSVC conditional patch from the earlier successful build without adapting it to subsequent source changes.

edges.comment: Issue c29, reporter yashamon's system: the reporter updated to newer source and explicitly reported that the previously successful local patch no longer worked there. The stale patch is therefore a known blind path for the newer checkout, even though it had worked on the earlier revision.

solution.intent: Integrate the MSVC-specific gettext stdint configuration fix into the current Neovim dependency build files, then ask the affected user to rebuild and verify it on native Windows ARM64 before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Port the tested MSVC branch to the current GettextCMakeLists layout, preserving stdint's uintmax_t definitions under MSVC instead of generating the incompatible fallback declarations. The maintainers later linked the merged implementation as PR #30679, but the reporter did not post a build result after that merge.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis is that Neovim's generated gettext configuration used fallback integer declarations incompatible with MSVC even though MSVC supplies suitable types through stdint.h. The raw C2632 log does not itself state that mechanism; it is inferred from the successful conditional patch and the final upstream fix.

edges.comment: Issue c29-c32. jxy-s submitted the updated fix and dundargoc reported that it should be fixed by the merged PR. No affected participant subsequently rebuilt current Neovim and confirmed the result, so the terminal state records the maintainer's resolution report without inventing user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Neovim's generated gettext configuration injected fallback intmax_t/uintmax_t declarations under MSVC despite the types being available through stdint.h, causing the ARM64 MSVC C2632 errors.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the native Hostarm64/arm64 compiler summary, the gettext stdint.h C2632 diagnostics, and the successful test of the MSVC-specific configuration patch.
Must not attribute the observed build failure to LuaJIT; an affected Windows ARM64 user built LuaJIT successfully, while the failing Neovim step was gettext.

Must not present the unchanged old local patch as sufficient for current source, because the reporter later observed that it no longer built the latest checkout; the fix must be integrated into the current gettext CMake layout.

Must ask the reporter to rebuild with a build containing the integrated gettext MSVC fix and verify the result before declaring the issue resolved; the thread ends with a maintainer saying the fix should be merged, not with an affected-user retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Initially inexperienced with CMake and Windows compiler targeting, but able to follow native-toolchain instructions, edit a CMake preset, apply a source patch, inspect compiler paths, and paste detailed build logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and exploratory; reports each new build result with raw errors, asks practical questions when blocked, and later shares concise instructions learned during troubleshooting.
